quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which one is NOT a way to stop a friend from driving while drunk?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with activities to slow their drinking and let them sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Ask other friends to help stop your friend from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To stop someone from drinking and driving, you can arrange a ride home, keep them busy with other activities, find an excuse to keep them from leaving, and get friends to help. Waiting 15 minutes does not work.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because drivers will see you easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This is where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally drunk.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.06 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legally drunk. It is illegal and unsafe to ride a motorcycle while drunk.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works well for maintaining close ranks and safe spacing. Use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Six times
20 times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets during a crash.

questions.question: How does the stopping distance for motorcycles compare to cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, slippery pavement makes stopping very difficult for motorcycles.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is never safe for motorcyclists.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane are safer.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area still provides enough grip for safe riding. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: Riders rarely hear a tire going flat. Tire failure is usually noticed by a change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Should be avoided because it can cause heat problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is light-colored.
Is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to their other safety benefits.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes suddenly while leaning.
Apply only the rear brake.
Apply only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, straighten the motorcycle and square the handlebars first, then stop. If you cannot straighten the motorcycle, apply the brakes slowly and gradually while reducing your lean, then apply more brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. If you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind, then slowly move forward.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Stop quickly right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both vehicles are stopped. The vehicle ahead could back up unexpectedly. You may also need space to move out of the way if another vehicle comes toward you from behind.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:

options.text: Remain in first gear.
Remain in neutral.
Remain in fifth gear.
Remain in any gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remain in first gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. When stopped, stay in first gear so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or place them in saddlebags. Piling loads on a sissy bar or frame is dangerous because it raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and changes the balance. Spread loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a motorcycle rider do?

options.text: Reduce their speed when riding at night.
Sound their horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Not ride at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle to be seen in their headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes reducing your speed, increasing your following distance, using other vehicles' headlights to see ahead, using your high beam headlight (unless passing or meeting another vehicle), and adjusting your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When may you not need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery
When there is a lot of traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
When it is raining

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Increase it if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if heavy traffic means another driver may pull in front of you.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane so others can see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best or should always be avoided. Change your position as needed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: Base travel distances on the least experienced rider.
Minimize breaks so the group reaches their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Use a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Minimize breaks so the group reaches their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Base route length on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind leaders so they can be watched. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Move onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side nearest the passing driver increases collision danger. Riding on the far side may make them return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right part of the lane so they see you in their mirror.
Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of the lane so they see you in their mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, move to the left part of your lane to see ahead better and to make yourself more visible. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar when a motorcycle accelerates?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is speeding up faster than the motorcycle.
It vibrates out of control.
It makes acceleration feel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to the motorcycle. Because of inertia, it will feel like it is falling behind when you speed up.

questions.question: Why do motorcycles seem to move faster than they actually do?

options.text: They appear to be going faster than they really are.
They appear to be going slower than they really are.
They appear to be stopped when they are moving.
They appear to be closer than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They appear to be going faster than they really are.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small. Because of their size, they may look like they are going faster than they actually are.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group ride?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
Toward the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride right behind the leader. This way, they do not have to work hard to keep up with the group. More experienced riders behind them can also watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should keep under normal conditions?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least a two-second distance behind the vehicle ahead of you. Increase this distance if conditions are bad, such as in rain or heavy traffic.

questions.question: What should you do with your body during a slow, tight turn?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean the opposite way from the motorcycle and the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean at the same angle as your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans to balance it.
